items.title: Charlie De Vore Interview, 1962-07-04
items.q: And like Tom says too, you can get, you don't have to worry so much about making fast runs if fingering and that type of thing. And you can think of more tasty things to do. That's what he said in essence.

ctx.x: Say we've got Paul setting them up like that. What about having guest lecturers?

That's invaluable because for instance you have maybe Jim Robinson come by. He hears the band and you've set the band up and you've got this so far. You've got a blues going medium tempo and you've got everybody doing this. Very simple and it would be very stiff. Then you slip Jim in there and say Jim this is with the band. What would you do playing along with us? The tromboman would drop out and Jim would start playing and he was going all the things that Jim does. Then a tromboman could really begin to get some…
that some of the New Orleans guys are pretty good talkers too.
